newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia plans rain-making for dry areas.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia plans rain-making for dry areas.

text.p: Indonesia plans to step up artificial rain-making efforts to help farmers cope with water shortages during the annual dry season, the official Antara news agency reported on Wednesday.
Public Works Minister Radinal Moochtar said more dams also would be built to store rain water until the next wet season.

Moochtar said priority would be given to key rice-growing areas of Java and South Sulawesi. Data from his ministry showed the current drought was having a greater impact on rice fields than previously predicted, he said.
Up to this week, 112,889 hectares (282,220 acres) of rice fields had been affected by drought, he said.
But the affected areas were still smaller than those hit in the dry seasons of 1991 and 1994, he added.
